evidence: Calls FragmentOnBonds with an incompatible argument and then calls nonexistent Chem.MolFragmentToMol; both raise before the revised ring-system routine completes.
Passes None from failed molecule parsing to MolToSmiles, producing repeated Boost.Python ArgumentError exceptions.
Tests mutual whole-fragment substructure containment after ring fragmentation; the benchmark asks whether a ring system is newly constructed and ignores external substituent properties.
Checks for an acyl chloride, a primary amine, and an amide product independently, without establishing that the detected atoms participate in the same transformation.
Constructs its own SMARTS and invokes RunReactants for membership; later fallbacks use independent reactant and product substructure flags.
Uses a short fixed list of aromatic SMARTS for four ring systems and supplements it with literal aromatic-token checks; valid representation variants are consequently missed.
Uses two hand-written quinoline and two hand-written indole SMARTS as gates before chain assembly, restricting accepted scaffold representations.
Ranks terminal products using coarse properties such as Boc presence, halogen count, and aromatic nitrogen count instead of testing exact target compatibility.
Repeatedly searches for any aminopyrimidine product with a free amine that could undergo acrylamide coupling; it never reaches a scored final answer before the execution limit.
